recipes.name: Easy Bacon, Onion, and Cheese-Stuffed Burgers
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound bacon, cut into 1/4 inch pieces

steps.text: Mix ground beef, barbecue sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt in a large mixing bowl, using your hands. Shape a small handful at a time (approximately 1/4 pound) into 12 thin patties. Lay patties out on a cookie sheet and cover with plastic wrap; place patties in the refrigerator.

Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 5 minutes. Remove bacon from skillet with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Reduce the heat to medium and cook onions in remaining bacon drippings until soft and just beginning to brown. Mix onions and bacon in a small bowl.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Meanwhile, remove beef patties from the refrigerator; top 6 patties with 1- 1/2 tablespoons of bacon and onion mixture, and sprinkle with shredded cheese. Top each with one of the remaining patties and press the edges together to seal.

Grill stuffed patties until beef is no longer pink in the center, about 4 to 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C). Serve on hamburger buns with condiments of your choice.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Bacon, Onion, and Cheese-Stuffed Burgers
raw_recipe.description: These juicy cheese-stuffed burgers with bacon and onion are full of savory flavor and can be grilled or pan-fried for a family-pleasing meal.

review.reviewBody: So filling and delicious! I pressed the hamburg as thin as possible and made equal sized patties. Next time, I think I'll deliberately make two diffent sized patties, putting my filling on the smaller one, and topping with the larger hamburger patty to make more secure topper and edge. I omitted the BBQ sauce (not a bit fan of it) and added the slightest bit of powdered garlic. For the life of me I can't grill hamburgers without their falling into the flame, so I pan-fried these and it worked wonderfully. Boyfriend raved about how good these are and I agree. Thank you for a fun, different and tasty way to make hamburgers!

Made these burgers twice in one week!
I prepped (16) 5" wide patties and chilled in fridge while preparing the rest.
I believe I made minor changes to this recipe.
I used a full pound of cooked bacon, but did not mix it with the cooked onions.
After cooking onions in bacon grease, I placed several paper towels on top of onions (and then discarded) to get rid of excess grease. 
I allowed onions to fully cool. Then divided among 8 patties evenly. 
I divided cooked bacon among those 8 patties . . . 
and then divided EXTRA Sharp Cheddar cheese (shredded)on top of the 8 patties.
I sealed the edges well and refrigerated for at least 1/2 hour.
Hubby grilled and all raved! Somehow with 8 burgers . . . only 4 four were fed.
Tonight, I had to double this recipe.
They could not wait for the burgers to be cooked quickly enough!
Totally Awesome!!!
I think it's important to allow all cooked ingredients (bacon and onions) to cool fully before assembling burgers . . . and especially allow burgers to be refrigerated at least 1/2 hour prior to grilling. This will help keep burgers from falling apart in the grilling process.

While the taste is awesome, even though I did not add the cheese inside, but put it on top... it is a rather messy burger, and like many, it easily falls apart on the grill. So in concept it was delicious, but execution was problematic. I would suggest, sauteing the onions with the bacon, and draining on paper towels. Then incorporating the whole concoction together, mixing the beef, salt, pepper, bbq sauce, garlic powder and the sauteed onion and bacon together, form into individual patties, grill 2-3 minutes per side, and add a nice slice of your favorite cheese on top... Heck I would even cook up some extra bacon and add a slice or two on top of the burgers with the cheese. Add a nice butter toasted bun and some more bbq sauce, dang that does sound like a winner!!!

I never truly follow a recipe, but more so use them as idea guides. this is a great base recipe for stuffed burgers. I made these tonight, (my first time ever attempting to make stuffed burgers) and everyone loved them! I made a mixture of crumbled blue cheese, crumbled bacon and fresh shredded Swiss cheese and reserved some to melt on the top after cooking (on the stove) just for pretty (and tasty). Served the burgers on oven toasted ciabatta bread with condiments. I sliced onion for dressing up, rather than cooked inside because I mixed French onion soup mix into the ground beef.

Very good recipe. Made a few changes though. I added an extra 1/2 tsp. of salt, 1/2 tsp. season salt, and subbed 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce for part of the BBQ sauce. In the filling, I added 1 diced jalepeno pepper ( and 1/8 tsp. cayenne if isn't spicy enough), and used 1 cup of shredded cheese.

 

They were sure yummy!

My family loved these. I grilled on the stove and tried to make them as thin as possible. Next time I might buy a patty press. Others said the cheese seeped out so I tried the presliced cracker sized cheese and it worked perfect. These burgers had so much flavor. We had them on onion buns with grilled mushroom and a homemade onion ring to top it off. Yum

It is important to make your burgers thin and larger than normal. And you must chill them. I didn't add the barbecue sauce, just Worchestershire, ~1 tbsp/lb of meat, salt, pepper and garlic powder. Add your filling, press top burger into bottom together, and if it's chilled properly, you can pick the whole burger up and round the edges by patting and pinching. These were good on the grill, but cooked in a copper grilling pan. No loss of filling. Really good idea.

these were just awesome. only thing i did different was i used a pack of onion soup mix in the hamburger mixture and they turned out great. just make your patties real thin and definitely refrigerate a hour or so before cooking. seal your edges good by working edges with your fingers and use i clump of cold cheese in the middle and they come out perfect. thanx

I would have given this recipes 4.5 stars if I could. It was really delicious! We ate them too quickly to even take a picture. 

I used turkey meat and turkey bacon instead, red onion, smoked barbecue sauce, and a little more garlic. After stuffing them, I had to make the patties very thin and large because the first one didn't cook thoroughly, but they shrunk to an edible size. They did come apart a little at the edges at first but just pinch the edges very well and flip only once.

The boyfriend really, really liked them. Even the next day.

I thought these were very good! I made the burger part per my own personal burger recipe and then added the filling as suggested here. Also, next time I think I will try it using ground sirloin! Next time I will also make sure to make the patties a little thinner!
Very juicy and the kids ate it up! I added garlic to the onions and added more bbq sauce and don't regret it a bit!
Awesome
Delicious
Husband loved it. Good texture and taste.
Made no changes!! No complaints here!

Added a little worcheshire sauce. And crushed garlic

Definitely will fix it again!!
Everyone loved these - served on kaiser buns with a fruit salad and corn on the cob! Delish!
Delicious.. Will press patties thinner and wider next time
My family loved these burgers very much. I followed the recipe as written.
Pretty good burger, just make sure to seal the edges after placing the top patty or else it'll separate on the grill.
